snapshot.title: UPSC History: C.R. Formula, Wavell Plan & Cabinet Mission
snapshot.exam_hook: 🏔️ UPSC History Hook: 1944: C.R. Formula. 1945: Wavell/Shimla. 1946: Cabinet Mission. Grouping A,B,C: Cabinet. Jinnah: Direct Action. Nehru: Interim Gov.

quick_notes.title: C.R. Formula (1944)
quick_notes.detail: By Rajagopalachari. Suggested a plebiscite in Muslim-majority areas after independence if they wanted to separate. Jinnah rejected it as he wanted "Pakistan" first.
quick_notes.explanation: The C.R. Formula, proposed in 1944 by C. Rajagopalachari, an Indian political leader, aimed to address the demand for a separate Muslim state. It suggested that after India gained independence from British rule, a plebiscite, meaning a direct vote by the people in that area, would be held in districts where Muslims were a majority. If the majority in those districts voted to separate, they could form a separate nation. However, Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the leader of the All-India Muslim League, rejected this proposal because he insisted that the creation of Pakistan must be agreed to before any independence or plebiscite took place. Jinnah wanted the principle of Pakistan to be accepted first, not after independence. The formula failed because the two sides could not agree on the sequence of events.

quick_notes.title: Wavell Plan (Shimla Conference 1945)
quick_notes.detail: Proposed an Executive Council with equal representation for Caste Hindus and Muslims. Failed because Jinnah insisted that only the League could nominate Muslim members.
quick_notes.explanation: The Wavell Plan, also called the Shimla Conference of 1945, was a British proposal to create an Executive Council, which is like a temporary government cabinet, with equal numbers of seats for two groups: Caste Hindus, meaning all Hindus who are not from the Scheduled Castes (Dalits), and Muslims. This plan failed because Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the leader of the All India Muslim League, insisted that only his party, the Muslim League, had the right to choose all the Muslim members of this council. The Congress Party, which represented all Indians including many Muslims, refused to accept this demand, so no agreement was reached and the conference ended without a new government being formed.

quick_notes.title: Cabinet Mission (1946)
quick_notes.detail: Members: Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander. Proposed : 1. A United India (No Pakistan). 2. A weak Center. 3. Grouping of provinces (A, B, C).
quick_notes.explanation: Cabinet Mission (1946) was a group of three British ministers sent to India to discuss the transfer of power. The members were Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps

quick_notes.title: Direct Action Day (Aug 16, 1946)
quick_notes.detail: Called by Jinnah to press the demand for Pakistan. Led to horrific communal riots in Calcutta (Great Calcutta Killings) and Noakhali.
quick_notes.explanation: Direct Action Day, on August 16, 1946, was a protest called by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, the leader of the Muslim League, to forcefully demand the creation of a separate country called Pakistan. The word "communal" refers to conflicts between different religious communities, in this case between Hindus and Muslims. On that day, peaceful protests turned into terrible communal riots in the city of Calcutta (now Kolkata), known as the Great Calcutta Killings, where thousands of people were killed. The violence then spread to the Noakhali district in present-day Bangladesh, causing more deaths and suffering. This event showed how deep the divide between communities had become and pushed Britain and the Indian leaders closer to the partition of India in 1947.

quick_notes.title: Interim Government (1946)
quick_notes.detail: Headed by Jawaharlal Nehru. Muslim League joined later but only to obstruct. Proved that a coalition was impossible at that stage.
quick_notes.explanation: The Interim Government was a temporary government formed in India in 1946 to manage the country while it was transitioning from British rule to independence. It was headed by Jawaharlal Nehru, who served as the Vice President of the Executive Council, which was like a prime minister. The Muslim League, a political party that wanted a separate country for Muslims, initially refused to join but later agreed to participate, though their main goal was to disrupt the government's work. This experience showed that the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League could not work together in a coalition, meaning a joint government, because their goals were too different. As a result, it became clear that India would have to be divided into two separate nations: India and Pakistan.

topic_title: UPSC History: C.R. Formula, Wavell Plan & Cabinet Mission
lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Negotiations for Power'. With the war ending, the focus shifted to how power would be transferred. We study the C.R. Formula (the first attempt at an INC-League settlement), the Wavell Plan, and the final Cabinet Mission Plan (1946). For UPSC, focus on 'Why the Cabinet Mission was accepted and then rejected' and the significance of the 'Direct Action Day' called by Jinnah. This is the tragic march towards Partition.
